issues.t: Drive unit grinding or milling noise
issues.sym: A grinding, milling or droning sound from the rear that rises and falls with speed, most noticeable when speeding up or slowing down. Some cars also clunk when shifting between drive and reverse.
issues.why: Early Model S drive units (the motor, inverter and gearbox in one housing) often developed noise. Some cases were a loose cable or a differential that needed a shim; others needed a full replacement unit.
issues.next: Have Tesla or an EV specialist listen to it and read the drive unit data. A noise alone is not an emergency, but a unit that loses power or throws an error should be repaired before long trips.

issues.t: Door handles won't extend or open the door
issues.sym: The flush door handle doesn't pop out when you walk up or press it, or it extends but the door won't unlatch. You may have to get in through another door.
issues.why: The motorized handles use a small gear, motor, microswitches and a thin wiring harness inside each handle. The gear cracks and the wires or switches break from repeated movement.
issues.next: Report it before it gets worse; the handle usually fails on one door at a time. Independent shops and rebuild kits can repair the handle for much less than a new assembly.

issues.t: Touchscreen goes blank from worn memory chip (recall 21V-035)
issues.sym: The center screen reboots, goes black or freezes. You may lose the backup camera, defrost and defog controls, and some warning chimes.
issues.why: The 8 GB flash memory chip inside the media control unit (MCU1) wears out from constant writing. Once it is full of worn blocks the computer can't start properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Tesla replaces the memory board for free under it; if the screen is already failing, avoid driving where you'd need the defroster.

issues.t: Yellow border or bubbles on the screens
issues.sym: A yellow or dark band creeps in from the edges of the center screen, bubbles appear under the glass, or a sticky liquid seeps out. The instrument cluster can do the same.
issues.why: The adhesive between the display layers breaks down with heat and age.
issues.next: This is cosmetic at first, but the screen can become hard to read. Ask about a display replacement or an upgrade to the newer MCU2 computer, which owners often choose at the same time.

issues.t: Battery coolant heater fails
issues.sym: An alert that the battery can't be heated, slow charging or limited regenerative braking in cold weather, and sometimes a no-charge condition.
issues.why: The electric heater that warms the battery coolant on early cars fails, so the pack can't be warmed up in the cold.
issues.next: Have Tesla or an EV shop confirm the fault code. Park in a garage in winter until it is repaired, since a cold pack charges slowly.

issues.t: Onboard charger stops charging
issues.sym: The car won't charge from a home or destination charger, charges at a fraction of the usual speed, or shows a charging error. Supercharging may still work.
issues.why: The onboard charger that converts household AC power to DC for the battery fails, or one of its internal modules does.
issues.next: Try a different charger and cable first to rule them out. If AC charging still fails, the onboard charger needs diagnosis; DC fast charging can get you by in the meantime.

issues.t: DC-DC converter failure
issues.sym: Warnings about the 12-volt system, the 12-volt battery not charging, or the car shutting down.
issues.why: The DC-DC converter steps down the high-voltage battery to recharge the 12-volt battery and run the car's electronics. Several 2013 owners report it failing.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed promptly. Without the converter, the 12-volt battery drains and the car can stop working.

issues.t: Air suspension sags or fails
issues.sym: One corner or the rear sits low after parking, the compressor runs often or loudly, the body leans more in turns, or a suspension warning appears.
issues.why: The air springs in the struts crack and leak with age, which overworks the compressor until it fails. Control module faults can also disable the system.
issues.next: Check if the car sits level each morning. Get a leak test before the compressor burns out, and don't drive far on a fully deflated corner. Coil-spring conversion kits exist for 2012–2016 cars.

issues.t: Front control arms and links clunk
issues.sym: Clunks, creaks or knocks from the front over bumps, a loose feel, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The bushings and ball joints in the front upper and lower control arms and the rear trailing and sway-bar links wear early on this heavy car.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected and replace worn arms in pairs, followed by an alignment to protect the tires.

issues.t: 12-volt battery dies early
issues.sym: Warnings to replace the 12-volt battery soon, the car not waking up or unlocking, or a black screen and a car that won't go into drive.
issues.why: The small 12-volt battery that runs the computers and locks wears out every few years, sometimes much sooner. It is one of the most reported Model S repairs.
issues.next: Replace it as soon as the warning appears. If the car is dead, a jump to the 12-volt terminals behind the front trunk will usually wake it up.

issues.t: Parking brake caliper seizes
issues.sym: The parking brake won't release, a rear wheel drags or gets hot, or the parking brake light comes on.
issues.why: The small electric parking brake calipers on the rear wheels corrode and stick, especially in salted-road areas.
issues.next: Don't drive with a dragging brake. Have the rear calipers serviced, and in winter climates have the brakes cleaned and lubricated yearly.

issues.t: Panoramic roof leaks or rattles
issues.sym: Water drips at the C-pillars, into the rear hatch or onto the headliner after rain or washing; the sunroof may stick, sit crooked or make noise.
issues.why: Roof seals shrink or shift and drain paths clog. The sliding panoramic roof can also go out of alignment.
issues.next: Keep the drains clear and have the seals inspected as soon as you see water. Dry out wet carpets fast to protect wiring.

issues.t: Wind noise from doors and windows
issues.sym: Whistling or roaring at highway speed from a front door or window, or doors that need extra force to close.
issues.why: The frameless door glass and seals drift out of alignment, and some doors sag over time.
issues.next: Ask for a window recalibration and seal adjustment first. A sagging door needs a body shop to realign it.

issues.t: Charge port door or latch faults
issues.sym: The charge port door won't open or close, the cable won't lock in or release, or charging stops partway.
issues.why: The small motor, sensor or wiring for the charge port door and latch fails or corrodes.
issues.next: Try the manual release inside the trunk if the cable is stuck. Have the port motor, sensor and wiring checked.

issues.t: Headlight LED or daytime light failure
issues.sym: Part of a headlight goes dark, such as the LED running light strip, or a warning about a lamp appears.
issues.why: The LEDs and their circuit boards inside the sealed headlight fail and can't be replaced separately.
issues.next: Ask whether a repaired or used assembly is available as an option to a new headlight.

issues.t: Tire pressure monitor errors
issues.sym: A tire pressure warning or system error even though the tires are fine, or no pressure readings.
issues.why: Early tire pressure sensors and their receiver fail or stop talking to the car.
issues.next: Check pressures with a gauge. Replacing a single sensor is simple; several owners upgraded to newer sensors and a new receiver.

issues.t: Power steering bolts can corrode and break (recall 18V-204)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes much heavier, especially at low speed, or you hear a clunk from the steering rack.
issues.why: Aluminum bolts holding the power steering motor can corrode, mostly in cold, salted-road areas, and snap, which cuts power assist.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for the recall; Tesla replaces the bolts for free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recalls 17V-023, 18V-031, 19V-002)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash. The risk is only that metal fragments could hit people if the airbag deploys.
issues.why: These cars use Takata passenger airbag inflators that can break apart with age, heat and humidity.
issues.next: Check your VIN now and get the free replacement right away.

issues.t: Front seat belt may not be connected to pretensioner (recall 15V-780)
issues.sym: No symptom you can see in normal driving.
issues.why: Front seat belts may not have been attached properly to the outboard lap pretensioner and could come loose in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the belt connection inspected for free.

issues.t: Parking brake may not release or hold (recall 17V-260)
issues.sym: The parking brake won't release, or it won't stay applied.
issues.why: A small gear in the electric parking brake caliper can break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Tesla replaces both rear parking brake calipers for free.

issues.t: Wall charging adapter can overheat (recall 14V-006)
issues.sym: A hot plug, melted or scorched adapter, or burning smell when charging from a 240-volt NEMA 14-50 outlet.
issues.why: The NEMA 14-50 adapter for the mobile charger could overheat at the outlet.
issues.next: Make sure you have the updated adapter with the thermal fuse. Stop using any adapter that looks discolored.

issues.t: Front trunk can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The front trunk lid pops up at speed and blocks your view.
issues.why: A misaligned latch can stop the secondary frunk latch from catching, so the hood is held only by the main latch.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the frunk ever pops while driving, slow down and pull over safely.

issues.t: Power steering assist may cut out on rough roads (recall 22V-818)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly feels heavy after a pothole or rough patch.
issues.why: Electric power steering software could misread a sudden current spike and turn off assist.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Make sure your software is up to date; the fix is an over-the-air update.

issues.t: False collision warnings and sudden braking (recall 21V-846)
issues.sym: A forward collision warning or hard automatic braking with nothing ahead.
issues.why: A software communication error between chips could trigger false warnings or emergency braking.
issues.next: Install the latest software update. Keep a safe distance behind you and report any repeats to Tesla.

issues.t: Autosteer may not keep the driver engaged (recall 23V-838)
issues.sym: Autosteer can stay on even if you look away or don't hold the wheel enough.
issues.why: Driver monitoring checks were judged too weak to prevent misuse of Autosteer.
issues.next: Install the over-the-air update, and always keep hands on the wheel and eyes on the road when using Autopilot.

issues.t: Backup camera image slow to appear (recall 22V-169)
issues.sym: The rearview image is delayed or missing when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A software problem could delay the camera feed.
issues.next: Install the latest update and look over your shoulder until the image appears.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may not deploy correctly (recall 22V-104)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: The curtain airbag inflators may have been assembled incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN and book the free airbag replacement.

issues.t: Windshield defrost weak in cold weather (recall 22V-050)
issues.sym: Cabin heat and windshield defrost fade on cold days.
issues.why: A software fault could trap refrigerant in the heat pump's evaporator, cutting heat output.
issues.next: Install the update. Stop driving if fog or ice blocks your view.

issues.t: Touchscreen lags or reboots while fast charging (recall 22V-296)
issues.sym: The center screen becomes slow or restarts during or after Supercharging, which can delay the backup camera, defrost and turn signals.
issues.why: The computer's processor could overheat while fast charging.
issues.next: Install the over-the-air update.

issues.t: Driver airbag may tear when it deploys (recalls 21V-868, 24V-967)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: The driver airbag cushion may tear during deployment, reducing protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the driver airbag replaced for free.

issues.t: Front seat belts may detach from anchor (recall 23V-488)
issues.sym: No symptom you can see.
issues.why: The front belts may not be properly attached to the lap pretensioner anchors.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the belts inspected for free.

issues.t: Horn may not sound from wrong horn pad (recall 25V-172)
issues.sym: Pressing the horn pad doesn't sound the horn.
issues.why: An incorrect horn pad may have been fitted with the driver airbag.
issues.next: Test the horn and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Hood may not warn when unlatched (recall 24V-554)
issues.sym: No alert appears even though the front trunk is not fully closed.
issues.why: The hood latch switch may not detect an open hood.
issues.next: Install the update and press the frunk lid down firmly before driving.

issues.t: Rearview image lag or missing (recalls 24V-035, 26V-283)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture freezes, lags or doesn't appear in reverse.
issues.why: Software instability could delay or block the camera feed.
issues.next: Install the latest update and check behind you before backing up.

issues.t: Backup camera lost from a computer board short (recall 25V-002)
issues.sym: The rearview camera image disappears.
issues.why: A circuit board in the car's computer can short-circuit.
issues.next: Check your VIN; Tesla updates the software and replaces the computer if needed.
